宮古そば なかよし.name: Miyako Soba Nakayoshi
宮古そば なかよし.desc: An old-fashioned diner run single-handedly by a grandma. You can enjoy traditional-style Miyako soba, with a distinctive, slightly sweet soy-sauce-based broth and the toppings hidden under the noodles. A wide-ranging menu that also includes goat soba and curry.
t: *This article was created with AI (Claude 3.7 Sonnet), with some additions of my own.
This time I went to "Miyako Soba Nakayoshi" in Shimashi, Ginowan! I ate here in November 2024😄
Miyako Soba Nakayoshi
Miyako Soba Nakayoshi

"Nakayoshi" is on the ground floor of an apartment building, and its bright exterior in orange and yellow catches the eye. The noren (shop curtain) at the entrance reads "Miyako Soba Nakayoshi," and an "Open" sign was hanging too. Beer crates were stacked in front of the shop, giving it a somehow nostalgic look😌
Inside the shop
Inside the shop
Inside the shop

Step inside and you'll find an old-fashioned diner-style interior. All kinds of menu placards are posted on the walls, and I really got the feeling that this is a shop long loved by the locals🎫 It seems a grandma runs the place by herself, so you may need to be prepared to wait a little when it's busy.
Menu posted on the wall
Menu posted on the wall
Menu posted on the wall
Menu posted on the wall

Looking at the menu posted on the wall, there's plenty of variety, from standard dishes like "goat soba," "soki soba," and "vegetable soba" to "katsu curry" and "curry rice." Prices are reasonable too, in the ¥600 to ¥900 range👍 This time I decided to order the "Miyako soba" that's in the shop's name!

After a short wait, the "Miyako soba" arrived. At first glance it looks simple, like just noodles topped with green onion, but that's the hallmark of Miyako soba😄 The toppings are hidden at the bottom; digging around, I found braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) and fish cake (kamaboko).
Miyako soba, large ¥700
Miyako soba, large ¥700 (fish cake and braised pork belly were hiding under the noodles😄)

First, a sip of the broth. The color is a little dark, and it looks like the broth of Tojin soba. It gives a different impression from the bonito broth or pork bone broth of typical Okinawa soba. If anything, it's soy-sauce-based with a bit of sweetness, with a distinctive flavor a bit like chicken broth. This is Miyako soba with a unique broth🤔
Miyako soba, large ¥700

Next, the noodles. They're the thin, straight noodles characteristic of Miyako soba, with a softish texture😋 The braised pork belly hidden at the bottom had a firm chew, with a somewhat strong sinewy texture. The fish cake, though simple, makes a nice accent too.

I think this is a shop where you can enjoy Miyako soba in its true form. I was able to savor a flavor different from the Okinawa soba at other shops. Since the grandma runs it alone, things look a little hard when it's crowded, but I think it's a good shop where you can feel the local taste, all of that included. If you want to experience Miyako's food culture, please stop by😊
Rating (9/15): Just plain tasty. Everyone, please do pay a visit to "Miyako Soba Nakayoshi"! Next time I'll introduce yet another Okinawa soba shop, so stay tuned~🍜✨

From the menu, I decided to go with the shop's signature dish, the "original soki soba." It's a reunion after a full four years, since I ate it at the main shop in Nago! Looking forward to that old-fashioned taste, I entered the shop feeling excited.

The shop is spacious, with local TV shows playing and the history of Okinawa soba and the shop's commitments displayed on the walls; it really feels like "a diner rooted in the community"🏠. Not just tourists but plenty of local regulars were there too, and it left an impression how everyone was relaxing and enjoying their meal.
Inside the shop
Well, after a while the "original soki soba"🍜 arrived.
Original soki soba, large ¥960

A big chunk of meat is plopped right on top; the volume is huge and it's really impressive! When I took my first sip of the broth right away...✨ the richness of the pork bone comes through clearly, and a deep flavor spreads out.
Original soki soba, large ¥960
Next, a scoop of noodles. The house-made noodles here are thick, and while soft, they're characterized by a chewy, springy bounce.

And then the meat of the "soki," which you could call the star of this soki soba. Because it's slowly simmered in a secret sweet sauce, its soft, falling-apart texture is irresistible. The sweet-and-savory sauce has soaked in deeply, and with every bite umami overflows in your mouth. The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) in particular seem to melt the moment you put them in your mouth, and they go perfectly with the sauce. I guess this flavor is a skill that comes from many years of experience🤲.

The "original soki soba" from Gabusoka soba, tasted for the first time in four years, had the same reliable deliciousness as ever. There are no flashy twists or special surprises, but I felt that this "usual taste" is the reason it continues to be loved locally. It's no wonder so many regulars come, and this sense of reassurance is the very essence of Okinawa soba✨. It makes me feel relieved every time I visit.
Rating (9/15): Just plain tasty. It's ★3 in the sense of "reliable deliciousness." As a bowl you can eat with peace of mind and enjoy, I'm sure it will go on being loved for a long time😆

つるりんこう.desc: A neighborhood soba shop in a salmon-pink building in a residential area of Kaiho, Okinawa City. In a Showa-retro interior, you get a classic broth where the sweetness of pork bone is the star, with three bone-in pork ribs. The breadth of its menu, a hybrid of neighborhood diner and soba shop, is also part of the appeal.

I ate here in December 2024😄 Today I dropped by "Tsururinko," which stands alone in a residential area of Kaiho, Okinawa City, right at its 11 o'clock opening. The big signs "Oki," "na," "wa," "soba" displayed boldly on the salmon-pink building stand out even from afar; it truly has the air of a "neighborhood soba shop"😊.
Tsururinko
Tsururinko

The gradient noren at the entrance shades from red to golden yellow, and the red cut-out letters of the shop's name are a little Showa-retro and cute. Customers kept coming in one after another the moment it opened, and it warmed my heart to think, "Ah, this shop is loved by the locals."
Inside the shop

Step inside and you're welcomed by wood-grain wainscoting, a Showa-era tiled ceiling, and the soft glow of round rattan lamps. There's raised tatami seating in the back and table seating in the front, and both have a menu, a thermos of tea, and a large condiment holder, giving a reassuring feeling like being at your family home.
Menu posted on the wall
Menu posted on the wall

The wall is lined with wooden-board menus. Besides soki soba, braised pork belly soba, and vegetable soba, there are also champuru, tonkatsu sets, and even fried rice; I was impressed by the broad range, a hybrid of "neighborhood diner" and "soba shop"👍

Now, what I came for this time was the soki soba, large (¥780). Before long, the bowl arrived on a black square tray along with an empty small plate.
Soki soba, large ¥780

First, a spoonful of the broth. The sweetness of pork bone spreads gently, and there's a reassuring feeling that made me nod, "This is the classic...!" The aroma of the bonito broth is hidden well in the background, and the richness of the pork is the star.
Soki soba, large ¥780
The noodles are medium-thick and straight. They're cooked on the soft side.
The topping is three hefty bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki). The soki are seasoned firmly sweet with soy sauce and brown sugar. There's some sinewy texture and small bones.

Rating (9/15): Overall, the soki soba at "Tsururinko" may not be flashy, but it was a bowl full of reassurance, like "this is the daily soba of Okinawa City residents." The noodles are softish, the broth is mainly pork bone and lightly sweet, and the soki are sweet. I think it's a classic Okinawa soba😌

796（ナンクル）.desc: Provisional #6 (12/15, 3rd visit). The No.1 agu-broth shop, in Chuo, Okinawa City. A cloudy white broth that's pork-bone-based yet not too heavy, by far the creamiest and richest. It clings superbly to the thick, wavy noodles. There's also the famous soki soba and unusual monthly specials.
t: (3rd visit) This article was created with AI (Claude 4 Sonnet), with some additions of my own lol🍜✨ I ate here in December 2024.

This time I joined the Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally for the first time in a while, and revisited "796 (Nankuru)" in Chuo, Okinawa City, which I've already introduced among my recommended shops😊 This was my third visit here, and no matter how many times I eat it, it's reliably delicious; it's an Okinawa soba shop especially proud of its rich broth made with agu pork.
The Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally card. This time I revisited with this in hand

Menu: Butter Chicken Curry Soba, recommended 3-item set ¥1,280
December's monthly special Okinawa soba, "Hokkaido Charred Miso Butter Soba" ¥1,080
Explanation of the order sheet (a style where you choose your soba, noodles, meat, and toppings and fill them in)

This time I ordered the "soki soba" with a soft-boiled egg topping. I've had it several times before, so I waited in the shop for a while expecting its reliable deliciousness. Looking at the bowl when it was brought out, the rich-looking broth really whets the appetite🤤
Soki soba (soft-boiled egg topping) ¥1,080 (soki soba ¥980, soft-boiled egg ¥100)

First, as usual, I taste the broth. The pork bone broth based on agu pork is by far the creamiest and richest of all the Okinawa soba shops I've eaten at😋 When you take a sip, a mellow umami spreads out, and you can also taste the refined sweetness unique to agu pork. Despite being this rich, it isn't too heavy, and the exquisite balance that makes you want to drink it all to the last drop is wonderful. As a pork-bone-based Okinawa soba shop, I definitely think it's the most delicious.
Soki soba (soft-boiled egg topping) ¥1,080 (soki soba ¥980, soft-boiled egg ¥100)

Next, the noodles. These also have their reliably chewy texture and cling superbly to the rich broth. The thick, wavy noodles grab hold of the broth, so you can savor the umami of the agu broth with every bite. The noodle texture is the same as last time, with firm springiness yet a gentle mouthfeel, and delicious✨

This time I ordered a soft-boiled egg as a topping, but this turned out a bit disappointing😅 The egg was served cold, so the temperature difference with the piping-hot broth bothered me. The soft-boiled doneness was good, but I wish it had been served a little warmer.

As for the soki, compared to previous visits, some sinewy texture remained, and it felt a little lacking in that melt-in-your-mouth tenderness. I had the impression it used to be simmered softer, so maybe it comes down to cooking timing or individual variation.

Actually, this shop recently started selling online through an e-commerce site, so I once ordered enough for my family online and tried it at home. However, since it's shipped chilled, it couldn't match the freshly made deliciousness of eating it at the shop, and it felt pricey too💦 Okinawa soba really is best enjoyed piping hot at the shop.

Even so, the quality of the broth and noodles is as high as ever, and the rich deliciousness of the agu broth is something special you can't taste anywhere else. Even on my third visit, that deliciousness hasn't changed, and I can well understand why people want to come back😊

In the stamp rally you end up going around all sorts of shops, but having a delicious shop as a benchmark makes it easier to compare with other shops. Nankuru is definitely one of those benchmark shops.

Rating (12/15): Nankuru delivered reliable deliciousness again this time. The rich agu broth is superb as always, and it pairs perfectly with the noodles. The soft-boiled egg and the condition of the soki were a little disappointing, but overall I think it maintains a high level. When you're in the Okinawa City area, it's a recommended Okinawa soba shop I'd love for you to try at least once✨

当南食堂.name: Tonan Shokudo
当南食堂.area: Noborikawa, Okinawa City (near Southeast Botanical Gardens)
当南食堂.desc: A well-worn local diner right next to the entrance of Southeast Botanical Gardens. Famous for its old-fashioned soba in a clear, golden bonito broth and its distinctive "sake" and "vinegar" condiments that hit hard with chili.
t: *This article was created with AI (ChatGPT-4o), with some additions of my own lol
I ate here in November 2024😄 This time I went to "Tonan Shokudo" in Noborikawa, Okinawa City!🏮
The building on the right is "Tonan Shokudo." On the left is the entrance to Southeast Botanical Gardens😄
Tonan Shokudo (quite the "Kitanashulin" - a shabby-but-tasty spot (^0^;))
The shop's exterior is well-worn and has the air of a place long loved by locals. There's a parking lot too, so it's convenient to visit by car🚗
Entrance of Tonan Shokudo

When you open the glass door at the entrance, a fairly spacious interior with the warmth of wood opens up✨ The area around the counter feels a bit cluttered, but that has its own charm too. Handwritten menus line the walls, and there's a homey, very Okinawan atmosphere.
Inside the shop
Menu posted in the shop
This time I ordered the "soki soba (large)" from the menu!🍜
Soki soba, large ¥800
The soba that was brought out after a while looks simple, like old-fashioned Okinawa soba. The broth is a clear golden color, bonito-based🐟 It's pretty ordinary.
Soki soba, large ¥800

The noodles are medium-thick and gently wavy. Cooked on the soft side. Personally I like a bit more firmness, but this too gives a feeling of old-fashioned Okinawa soba🍜 However, even though I ordered a large, the amount of noodles felt small compared to other Okinawa soba shops🤔

The soki topping has a light seasoning and is understated. But when I ate it, it was quite sinewy, and my impression was it was mostly bone with little meat to eat🥩 I'd have been happier if it were simmered until falling-apart tender.

On the table were condiments labeled "sake" and "vinegar," so I tried them🔥 These are quite distinctive! The chili heat hits harder than regular kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori), and the vinegar's sourness is strong too🌶️ Adding them to the broth gives it a punchy flavor, so opinions may be divided, but I recommend them to people who like spicy food.
The shop was bustling with customers, and I could tell it's a popular diner👪
Overall, my impression was "plainly tasty Okinawa soba." It doesn't feel especially special, but the old-fashioned diner atmosphere and gentle flavor are its charms🌺
Rating (9/15): Overall my impression is "plainly tasty Okinawa soba," but I recommend it to anyone who wants to experience the atmosphere of an Okinawan diner loved by its customers!😊
